topic.name: Finding Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

question.text:
\[ \begin{vmatrix} 2 & -1 & -3 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{red}2 & \color{red}3 & \color{red}-2 \\ -3 & -2 & 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} \]

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of $a_{31}$ equal to zero.
question.explanation:
Let's make entries to the right of $a_{31}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}2 & -1 & -3 & -1 \\ \color{blue}-1 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{black}2 & \color{black}3 & \color{black}-2 \\ \color{blue}-3 & -2 & 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} C_2:=C_2+(-2)C_1 \\ C_3:=C_3+(-3)C_1 \\ C_4:=C_4+2C_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}2 & -5 & -9 & 3 \\ \color{blue}-1 & 3 & 7 & -1 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}-3 & 4 & 10 & -4 \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}2 & -5 & -9 & 3 \\ \color{blue}-1 & 3 & 7 & -1 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}-3 & 4 & 10 & -4 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}} \cdot (-1)^{3+1} \begin{vmatrix} -5 & -9& 3\\ 3 & 7 & -1 \\ 4 & 10 & -4 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} -5 & -9& 3\\ 3 & 7 & -1 \\ 4 & 10 & -4 \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

example.title: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Column Operations

question.text:
\[ \begin{vmatrix} 8 & -4 & 7 & -3\\ 2& -4 & -5 & 4 \\ \color{red}-2 & \color{red}4 & \color{red}-8 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} \\ 5 & 3 & 7 & -2 \end{vmatrix} \]

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left of $a_{34}$ equal to zero.
question.explanation:
Let's make entries to the left of $a_{34}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} 8& -4 & 7 & \color{blue}-3 \\ 2 & -4 & -5 & \color{blue}4 \\ \color{black}-2 & \color{black}4 & \color{black}-8 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} \\ 5 & 3 & 7 & \color{blue}-2 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} C_1:=C_1+C_4 \\ C_2:=C_2+(-2)C_4 \\ C_3:=C_3+4C_4 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 2 & -5 & \color{blue}-3 \\ 6 & -12 & 11 & \color{blue}4 \\ \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & \color{blue}-2 \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 2 & -5 & \color{blue}-3 \\ 6 & -12 & 11 & \color{blue}4 \\ \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} \\ 3 & 7 & -1 & \color{blue}-2 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2}} \cdot (-1)^{3+4} \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 2 & -5\\ 6 & -12 & 11 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= -2 \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 2 & -5\\ 6 & -12 & 11 \\ 3 & 7 & -1 \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

example.title: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Column Operations

question.text:
\[ \begin{vmatrix} 9 & 8 & -4 & -3 \\ 5 & -4 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & 0 & 1 & -1 \\ \color{red}-2& \color{red}-6 & \color{red}4 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} \end{vmatrix} \]

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left of $a_{44}$ equal to zero.
question.explanation:
Let's make entries to the left of $a_{44}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} 9 & 8 & -4 & \color{blue}-3 \\ 5 & -4 & -1 & \color{blue}3 \\ -3 & 0 & 1 & \color{blue}-1 \\ \color{black}-2 & \color{black}-6 & \color{black}4 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} C_1:=C_1+C_4 \\ C_2:=C_2+3C_4 \\ C_3:=C_3+(-2)C_4 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} 6 & -1 & 2 & \color{blue}-3 \\ 8 & 5 & -7 & \color{blue}3 \\ -4 & -3 & 3 & \color{blue}-1 \\ \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} 6 & -1 & 2 & \color{blue}-3 \\ 8 & 5 & -7 & \color{blue}3 \\ -4 & -3 & 3 & \color{blue}-1 \\ \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2}} \cdot (-1)^{4+4} \begin{vmatrix} 6& -1 & 2 \\ 8 & 5 & -7 \\ -4 & -3 & 3 \\ \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= 2 \begin{vmatrix} 6& -1 & 2 \\ 8 & 5 & -7 \\ -4 & -3 & 3 \\ \end{vmatrix}. \end{align*}

example.title: Reducing a 4x4 Determinant to a 3x3 Determinant Using Column Operations

question.text:
Calculate the value of $ \, \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 7 & -2 & 5 \\ 5 & -6 & 4 & 1\\ 4 & -4 & 2 & -2 \\ -6 & 1 & -3 & 3 \end{vmatrix}. $

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of $a_{33}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4 \times 4$ determinant to a $3 \times 3$ determinant.
question.explanation:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the left and to the right of $a_{33}=2$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 7 & \color{blue}-2 & 5 \\ 5 & -6 & \color{blue}4 & 1\\ 4 & -4 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & -2 \\ -6 & 1 & \color{blue}-3 & 3 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} C_1:=C_1+(-2)C_3 \\ C_2:=C_2+2C_3 \\ C_4:=C_4+C_3 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 3 & \color{blue}-2 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & \color{blue}4 & 5 \\ \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{red}0 \\ 0 & -5 & \color{blue}-3 & 0 \end{vmatrix} . \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 3 & \color{blue}-2 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & \color{blue}4 & 5 \\ \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{red}0 \\ 0 & -5 & \color{blue}-3 & 0 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2}} \cdot (-1)^{3+3} \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 3 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= 2 \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 3 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & 5 \\ \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-5} & \color{red}0 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= 2\cdot({\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{-5}}) \cdot (-1)^{3+2} \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 3 \\ -3 & 5 \end{vmatrix}\\[5pt] &= 10(25+9) \\[5pt] &= 340. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing 4x4 Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

question.text:
Calculate the value of $ \, \begin{vmatrix} 6 & -12 & -2 & -7 \\ 2 & -6 & -2 & -4 \\ -4 & 12 & 7 & 8 \\ -3 & 4 & 4 & 2 \end{vmatrix}. $

Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of $a_{21}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4 \times 4$ determinant to a $3 \times 3$ determinant.
question.explanation:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the right of $a_{21}=2$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}6 & -12 & -2 & -7 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & -6 & -2 & -4 \\ \color{blue}-4 & 12 & 7 & 8 \\ \color{blue}-3 & 4 & 4 & 2 \end{vmatrix} && \qquad \begin{array}{l} C_2:=C_2+3C_1 \\ C_3:=C_3+C_1 \\ C_4:=C_4+2C_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}6 & 6 & 4 & 5 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}-4 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ \color{blue}-3 & -5 & 1 & -4 \end{vmatrix} . \end{align*}

Expanding the result along the $2$nd row, we get

\begin{align*} & \:\,\phantom{=} \begin{vmatrix} \color{blue}6 & 6 & 4 & 5 \\ \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2} & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 & \color{red}0 \\ \color{blue}-4 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ \color{blue}-3 & -5 & 1 & -4 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= {\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{2}} \cdot (-1)^{2+1} \begin{vmatrix} 6 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & -4 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= - 2\cdot \begin{vmatrix} 6 & 4 & 5 \\ \color{red}0 & \color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{3} & \color{red}0 \\ -5 & 1 & -4 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= (-2) \cdot ({\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{3}}) \cdot (-1)^{2+2} \begin{vmatrix} 6 & 5 \\ -5 & -4 \end{vmatrix}\\[5pt] &= -6(-24+25) \\[5pt] &= -6. \end{align*}
